2aaf268658ecf0cab2db0e30: Delivery: A scope sheet and a table faithful to the requests received.
6e27cd5c1358215cf15f426b: **Why learn:** A concrete output lets you compare the request with the result. Without that comparison, a well-written response can look finished even when important information is missing.
bc201ee17d7d4ba56ad30306: **Key concepts:** Input: Material available before the task; Output: File or result to deliver; Unit: What each item represents; Scope: Limit of the transformation
bc6ab9acb68b105f9de796ce: **Why learn:** The sheet reduces back-and-forth and helps identify scope changes. A new function joins a future list instead of silently altering the work in progress.
d9147fdf916060332144191a: **Key concepts:** Goal: A sentence with a verb and a result; Exclusion: What is left for later; Acceptance: An observable condition of success; Pending item: Necessary data that is still missing
e6107f42ad3862335d46a25f: **Why learn:** The quality of the output depends on how clearly the transformation is specified. Handling the gaps is usually more useful than adding adjectives like perfect, complete, or professional.
b8ceb1697394182d82f0d4d9: **Key concepts:** Format: Expected columns and organization; Fidelity: Preserve what was received; Gap: Information that wasn’t provided; Separation: Distinguish instructions from data
682429fe737063edfd33ab27: **Why learn:** Verification turns an impression into evidence. It also shows what to fix: in extraction, format, or business rule—without rebuilding the entire process.
a44479e3bb9c103aa612d599: **Key concepts:** Count: Expected number of records; Match: Field linked to the correct order; Regression: An old error that comes back; Evidence: Preserved input and output
704f26cc8116c088364de0a2: ### 5. Close one step at a time
fad6b03bccde566d6cc6ca6a: **Why learn:** Limiting work in progress reduces the feeling of having many projects almost done. You end up accumulating small deliveries that work and can be combined.
ba0f3650ed6387c3cef59b70: **Key concepts:** Step: Part with an independently achievable result; Limit: One active delivery at a time; Blocker: Identified dependency; Improvement: An idea outside the current scope
8324a17a5112971c7c83a7ef: **Why learn:** Practice teaches you to close a small task and introduces a central idea from the course: vary the input to see whether the solution understood the rule or just copied the example.
aae9f8359c3c5469f45a5066: **Key concepts:** Common case: Order with all fields; Incomplete case: Order without a deadline; Variation: Change one piece of data and repeat; Conclusion: Compare and save the result

3bf8a2cb293fae072236e888: **Key concepts:** Review: A specific state of the code; Installer: A routine that alters the environment; Target: Folders and services affected; Record: A decision tied to evidence

13c4105bc7edb1812205a3ac: **Key concepts:** Evidence: A snippet that can be located; Impact: The consequence if the behavior occurs; Context: Execution conditions; Triage: Classify and justify the finding

4d9efa4305e6410cdb35b04b: **Key concepts:** Confirmed: Demonstrated behavior; False positive: A pattern without the claimed risk; Inconclusive: Insufficient evidence; Focused test: An experiment that resolves the doubt
1398c671493b96d76dc134a5: **Why learn:** Testing reduces the cost of discovering incompatibilities. You learn how the system behaves before allowing it into bigger tasks or using important documents.
f819498928acc9c25c8434a9: **Key concepts:** Isolation: Limit the test scope; Fixture: A fictitious verification input; Reversal: How to go back to the previous state; Promotion: Expand usage after validating
9f2fe75ad5fa399d9f708875: **Why learn:** A well-written decision can be reviewed by someone else. It also shows that inspection isn’t a final stamp: new behaviors require new analysis.
021344e989a549190b6575a2: **Key concepts:** Statement: What the tool promises; Observation: What the code does; Condition: What needs to change; Decision: Use, restrict, or defer
01041d75a32889ec13004bc5: Delivery: A short report with a reproduced problem and its minimal fix.
8042aa4b1660871e437ab453: **Why learn:** Context reduces generic comments and prevents the reviewer from proposing changes that contradict the goal. It also limits the cost and scope of the review.
077ff156dcdfe24ac8f5c355: **Key concepts:** Contract: Expected behavior; Diff: Difference between versions; Hypothesis: A possible problem to investigate; Reproduction: Steps that show the effect
50a950ecf4269e8c67fb9a1f: **Why learn:** A clear baseline prevents the reviewer from comparing the wrong files or treating old code as part of the current change. Checking status also avoids accidentally publishing preparation data.
f7aa800ed52e012b64589afe: **Key concepts:** Baseline: Version used for comparison; Status: New and modified files; Scope: The set to review; Local help: Contract of the installed CLI
084cb661806dddf7570b95e0: **Why learn:** Actionable findings turn the review into a decision-making tool. You can prioritize by impact and verify whether the smallest change actually resolved the case.
7774261c72e5661103dc1def: **Key concepts:** Trigger: Condition that starts the failure; Effect: Observed result; Priority: Impact and likelihood; Minimal fix: Change sufficient to resolve
81a3c3efe2b9dd908d023aa0: **Why learn:** These scenarios are easy to forget in demonstrations. Testing repetition and interruption reveals problems that a superficial reading or a single run doesn’t show.
faeb46e7a4d1198c8ca1a4e8: **Key concepts:** Retry: A new attempt of the same operation; Idempotency: Repeat without duplicating the effect; Atomicity: Complete everything or don’t apply; Interruption: Failure between steps
ca44327f23ef88c97b0f742e: **Why learn:** A minimal case reduces the number of possible explanations. It allows you to distinguish a logic problem, an incompatible configuration, and an unavailable dependency.
95ccf64404a950b73a75a039: **Key concepts:** Minimal case: Smallest input that keeps the failure; History: Attempts and results; Single hypothesis: One tested cause at a time; Stop condition: An objective condition for completion
2a597ef20060808ccbc40db6: **Why learn:** Practice connects review, testing, and business behavior. You learn to check the real effect of the fix and to recognize when two seemingly identical inputs represent different situations.

b7eb9a1c693f4e1a1ab7aefd: **Why learn:** A general benchmark doesn’t tell you whether your specific table format will be preserved. A test with a representative sample leads to a decision suited to your case.

c22907e2c6c46396edb37e8e: ### 3. Use Markdown as a readable structure
1ca119968d7522c9c8615ef9: **Why learn:** Explicit structure helps you locate information and reduces ambiguity. A number without its heading can be interpreted incorrectly even when it was extracted correctly.
bc579452debfa0fffd0052c7: **Key concepts:** Title: Indicates topic and hierarchy; List: Groups related items; Table: Relates column and value; Note: Condition that changes interpretation
f996af04635a8db1e7967996: **Why learn:** Structure errors are subtle and can contaminate later analyses. Checking a few critical cells identifies issues that don’t show up when counting characters or pages.
94fa42d9409e8cbf458d3def: **Key concepts:** Header: Defines the column’s meaning; Unit: Scale associated with the value; Decimal: Separator that changes the number; Formula: Calculation rule, not just the result
0f87ff01265d8b9f35cea0e6: **Why learn:** Traceability lets you answer where an information came from. It also prevents converting identical files repeatedly or continuing to use an old version without realizing it.
